Monday. In the canteen Rohit leaned over. “Did you know Seema failed her viva and lied to everyone about it?” Hemant said nothing, but his tea went cold.

Wednesday. Hemant kept thinking about it. He was curious, and a little hurt that his friend Seema hadn't told him. But she had helped him with his lab file all last semester. He decided not to repeat it to anyone.

Friday. After class he said, “Seema, someone told me something about your viva. I don't want to guess. Can I ask you?” She sighed. “I asked for a re-evaluation because the marking was off. I didn't tell people because I hadn't heard back.” She gave a tired smile. “Thanks for asking me instead of them.”

qa.q: What did Rohit say about Seema?
qa.a: Rohit said Seema failed her viva and lied to everyone about it.

qa.q: What was Hemant feeling on Wednesday, with curiosity and loyalty pulling apart?
qa.a: Hemant felt curiosity and a little hurt, but also loyalty to Seema, who had helped with the lab file.

qa.q: What choice did Hemant make on Friday?
qa.a: Hemant asked Seema directly instead of guessing or repeating it.

qa.q: What might Seema have felt when Hemant said someone had told something about the viva?
qa.a: Seema likely felt a jolt of worry, then relief that Hemant came to Seema first; the tired smile hints at weariness.

grounding: A student is told something unflattering about a friend and, feeling curiosity and loyalty, checks with Seema directly.

passage:
Hafsa, you look worried about that message. Let me tell you what happened to me. I'm Shankar. In my second year a boy at our hostel mess table told me that my friend Venu was borrowing money from everyone and never paying it back. Half of me wanted to know more. The other half remembered Venu carrying my trunk up four floors the day I arrived.

So I didn't repeat it. That night I sat with Venu and said, “Someone told me something. I'd rather hear it from you.” Venu went quiet, then said, “I borrowed for my father's hospital bills, and I've repaid all but one person.” Then, softly, “Thank you for asking before believing it.”

I still ask first, Hafsa. Try it once.

qa.q: What did the boy at the mess table say about Venu?
qa.a: The boy said Venu was borrowing money from everyone and never paying it back.

qa.q: What was Shankar feeling, with curiosity and loyalty pulling in two directions?
qa.a: Shankar felt curiosity to hear more and loyalty because Venu had carried the trunk up four floors.

qa.q: What choice did Shankar make that night?
qa.a: Shankar sat with Venu and said Shankar would rather hear it from Venu.

qa.q: How might Venu have felt when a friend asked instead of believing the rumour?
qa.a: Venu probably felt anxious at first, then relieved and grateful that Shankar asked before judging.

grounding: An elder recalls being told something unflattering about a friend, feeling curiosity and loyalty, and checking with the friend directly.

passage:
It was exam week, the library was packed, and Uma had two assignments due by midnight. In the queue for the photocopier, Mehul leaned over. “You know Hrithik copied your case study last term? He showed it to Ritika like it was his.”
Uma felt a jolt. Hrithik, her project partner for two years?
Part of her wanted every detail. Who saw it? When? Another part wanted to shut Mehul up.
She took her photocopies and said, “I'll ask him myself.” She had forty minutes before the next deadline.
She found Hrithik in the canteen and asked straight: “Did you show my case study as yours?”
He looked shocked. “No! I showed her yours as an example of a good one. I said it was yours.”
Uma let out a long breath.

qa.q: What did Mehul say Hrithik copied?
qa.a: He said Hrithik copied her case study last term.

qa.q: What did Uma feel pulling her in different directions after Mehul spoke?
qa.a: She felt curious, wanting every detail, but also loyal to Hrithik and wanting to shut Mehul up.

qa.q: Why was asking Hrithik directly a good choice, even under time pressure?
qa.a: It got the real story from the source quickly and kept their trust intact instead of letting gossip decide.

qa.q: How might Hrithik have felt when Uma asked?
qa.a: He looked shocked and was probably hurt that such a story was going around, but glad she asked him directly.

grounding: Shows a student hearing gossip about a friend, torn between curiosity and loyalty, choosing to check with the friend directly.

passage:
At the college canteen, over samosas, Deepak lowered his voice. “Tejas, did you hear? Your friend Saurabh got thrown out of his internship. Something about fake bills.”
Tejas put down his cup. Saurabh? Who never even took extra ketchup packets?
“Who told you?”
“Everyone's saying it.”
Tejas felt a strong pull to ask more, to hear every juicy detail. Then he thought of Saurabh's face if he heard Tejas had been gossiping.
That evening he messaged Saurabh: “Hey, heard some weird stuff about your internship. Didn't believe it. You okay?”
Saurabh called within a minute. “They cut the internship short for everyone. Budget. That's all. Who's saying fake bills?”
“Nobody important,” Tejas said. “Want to get dinner?”

qa.q: What did Deepak say Saurabh was thrown out for?
qa.a: He said something about fake bills.

qa.q: What was Tejas feeling as he heard the rumour?
qa.a: He felt curious, pulled to hear every detail, but also loyal and uneasy about gossiping about his friend.

qa.q: What did Tejas do that kept trust intact?
qa.a: He checked with Saurabh privately and said he didn't believe it, which let Saurabh explain the real reason.

qa.q: How might Saurabh have felt hearing about the rumour?
qa.a: Saurabh was probably surprised and upset, but grateful that Tejas asked directly.

grounding: Shows a student hearing unflattering gossip about a friend and choosing to check with him directly, keeping trust intact.

passage:
“Rajni, I have to tell you something,” said Pallavi in the hostel corridor. “Jahnavi told the girls in 204 that you're fake and only friends with her for her notes.”
Rajni felt her face go hot. “She said that?”
“That's what I heard.”
Rajni wanted to ask who else was there, what else Jahnavi said. Instead she knocked on Jahnavi's door.
“Can I ask you something straight? Did you tell 204 I'm only your friend for notes?”
Jahnavi's eyes went wide. “What? No! I said you're the only one who ever returns my notes on time.”
They stared at each other. Then both burst out laughing.
“Pallavi,” said Jahnavi. “She hears everything wrong.”

qa.q: Which room's girls did Pallavi mention?
qa.a: The girls in 204.

qa.q: How did Rajni feel when Pallavi told her?
qa.a: She felt hurt and curious, her face going hot, wanting to know more.

qa.q: Why was going straight to Jahnavi a wise choice?
qa.a: It cleared up a misunderstanding quickly and kept their friendship intact, instead of letting the gossip grow.

qa.q: How might Jahnavi have felt hearing what was said about her?
qa.a: Jahnavi was probably shocked and a bit hurt, then relieved when they sorted it out and laughed.

grounding: Shows a student told something unflattering about a friend, torn between curiosity and loyalty, choosing to check with the friend directly.

passage:
I'm Zubin, and last month I nearly lost a friend over one sentence.
A few of us from drama club were in the canteen when Kunal said, "You know Shreya only got the lead because she's the director's cousin?" Everyone looked at me, because Shreya and I have been close since first year.
Part of me badly wanted to know if it was true. I even felt a flicker of "that explains it." Then a heavier feeling, like I was betraying her just by listening. I said, "I don't know that," and left my tea.
That evening I asked her straight: "People are saying you're related to the director. Is that true? I'd rather hear it from you."
She laughed, then went quiet. "He's my neighbour's son. I auditioned three times." Then she hugged me. "Thanks for asking me instead of them."

qa.q: What did Kunal claim about how Shreya got the lead?
qa.a: That she got it because she's the director's cousin.

qa.q: What mixed feelings did Zubin have while listening to Kunal?
qa.a: Zubin felt curious, even a flicker of "that explains it", but also guilty, as if just listening betrayed Shreya.

qa.q: Why was checking with Shreya the wise choice?
qa.a: It got the facts from the person concerned, so Zubin didn't spread or believe a false story, and it kept their trust.

qa.q: How did Shreya feel about Zubin asking her directly?
qa.a: Shreya seemed hurt for a moment, then grateful, and hugged Zubin for asking her instead of the others 🤍

grounding: Shows a student told something unflattering about a friend, torn between curiosity and loyalty, choosing to check with the friend directly.
